subject: Vendor roster assurance & egress path details requested by BigBank
messages:
From: Alex Dillon <alex.dillon@bigbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: vendor roster + egress path assurance for upcoming audit

Hannah,

We are preparing for our internal third-party audit next month and need a short, formal response from Redwood covering: the current list of subprocessors that touch production customer data, the cloud operator(s) used per region, and any outgoing egress IP ranges or public endpoints that BigBank should allow for webhook callbacks or telemetry.

Specifically we need: 
- CSV roster with vendor name, role (subprocessor/type), region(s) where they operate, and contract link or effective date.
- A diagram or list enumerating egress destinations (cloud provider egress ranges, external vendors, CDN/monitoring endpoints) and whether TLS / mTLS are enforced.
- Any planned changes to operators in the next 90 days that could affect data residency.

Can you provide a response (and attachments) by EOD 2026-08-20? If there are any items we can redact, please call that out.

Thanks,
Alex Dillon
Third-Party Risk Manager
BigBank, Inc.

Subject: RE: Request: vendor roster + egress path assurance for upcoming audit

Alex — attaching the requested materials. Quick summary up front:

1) Subprocessor roster (attached: subprocessor_roster_v1.csv) — contains vendor name, primary role (e.g., object storage, edge operator, monitoring), regions where they have production access, and effective DPA execution date. We have redacted vendor contact email addresses per contract. If you need contract PDFs we can provide them under NDA separately.

2) Egress mapping (attached: egress_map_diagram.pdf) — shows traffic flows for eu-west-1 and us-central-1, plus a consolidated list of public egress destinations:
   - NorthStar Cloud (edge operator): eu-west-1 — egress ranges listed on page 2 of the PDF; we enforce TLS 1.2+ on all control plane and data-plane connections, and mTLS for internal service-to-service telemetry.
   - FastCDN (CDN): outgoing webhook callbacks may use FastCDN public endpoints; we recommend allowing the FQDNs listed in the diagram.
   - Monitoring/observability endpoints (third-party): Prometheus remote write targets are behind private network paths to NorthStar; alerting webhooks go to external vendor endpoints over HTTPS.

3) Planned changes: no operator changes are scheduled in the next 90 days for eu-west-1. We do have a planned minor routing config change on 2026-09-05 (non-residency affecting) that will shift telemetry egress to a bonded transit through NorthStar — details included in the diagram.

4) Security controls: all vendor connections use at-rest encryption (AES-256) and TLS in transit. We maintain per-vendor IAM roles and short-lived credentials (rotated); audit logs are retained per our policy (90 days for operational logs, longer for compliance artifacts).

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v1.csv (CSV roster, redacted contact columns), egress_map_diagram.pdf (diagram + egress ranges table).

Next steps: if you need signed DPAs or redacted contract extracts, we can route those via Vendor Contracts (legal@redwood.com) — let me know and I'll coordinate.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference
